 LITTLE ROCK (KATV) — A new federal lawsuit is challenging restrictions on what Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) recipients can purchase with their benefits in Arkansas and 17 other states.
 The class-action lawsuit was filed on Nov. 18 by the National Center for Law and Economic Justice. It asks a federal court to overturn U.S. Department of Agriculture-approved waivers that prohibit SNAP recipients from purchasing certain foods and beverages.
 Arkansas is among the 18 states targeted. The restrictions vary by state but generally prohibit purchases of products such as soda, candy, energy drinks and certain prepared desserts.
 This comes after a USDA-approved waiver from Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders banned SNAP recipients in the state from using their benefits to purchase soda (including low- and no- calorie varieties), candy, energy drinks and certain prepared deserts. Those restrictions took effect on July 1, 2026.
 Gov. Sanders' office called this reform plan an attempt to restore food stamps' focus on nutrition, tying the effort to a broader national health initiative aligned with the “Make America Healthy Again” campaign.
 RELATED | Arkansas SNAP ban on soda and candy takes effect under Sanders waiver 
 It is crazy that hardworking taxpayers pay for the soft drinks and junk food that make people unhealthy and then pay for the healthcare those people need to get better. Arkansas is fixing that broken system,” said Governor Sanders a July press conference. “Government programs need to recognize the link between nutrition and health, which is why Arkansas is leading with common sense and making this long overdue change to our food stamp program. The lawsuit argues that the USDA exceeded its legal authority by approving the waivers, which allow states to change the definition of eligible food under the federal nutrition assistance program.
 The plaintiffs also argue the agency did not follow required procedures before approving the restrictions and that the varying rules have created confusion for SNAP recipients and retailers.
 According to the lawsuit, some recipients rely on products affected by the restrictions to manage chronic health conditions or meet other nutritional needs. The complaint also raises concerns that retailers could face penalties or lose their authorization to accept SNAP benefits if they unintentionally allow prohibited purchases.
 The other 17 states included in the lawsuit are Florida, Hawaii, Idaho, Indiana, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Montana, Nevada, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Texas, Utah, Virginia and Wyoming.
 The Arkansas Department of Human Services recently launched a SNAP Companion App, which allows recipients to scan bar codes to see if specific food items are eligible for purchase with their benefits.

 The filing does not immediately change Arkansas' SNAP restrictions. They remain in effect unless a court issues an order or state or federal officials take further action.
 The USDA has defended the waivers as a way to give states more flexibility to encourage healthier food choices among SNAP recipients.
